findings.observation: B’s featured player occupies most of the desktop opening, leaving no readable license condition or pack choice in the capture. On mobile, the waveform precedes the sample title and play action by roughly 200 pixels.
findings.impact: The featured cue separates audition from the rights and scope decisions. B misses the explicit desktop requirement despite making its first sample available within the mobile opening.
findings.repair: Retain B’s prominent cue treatment within A’s compact browser-and-rail structure. Place readable license conditions and the start of pack choice beside it on desktop; group the title, play action and waveform together on mobile. Recheck at these same viewport sizes.

findings.observation: A provides the stronger decision surface, but its subject-specific material remains confined to thin waveform strips inside conventional rows. The oversized general headline and team callout carry less identity than B’s coral waveform, dark listening surface and cue-specific description.
findings.impact: A resolves the opening’s practical arrangement more convincingly than its expressive direction. Expanding it unchanged would underuse the supplied sound material; choosing B unchanged would sacrifice useful decision adjacency.
findings.repair: Develop a compact synthesis before expansion: preserve A’s scanable sample list and decision rail while giving the selected cue B’s stronger waveform presence and contextual writing. Recover space from the general introduction rather than enlarging the whole browser. Verify that the material remains distinctive while samples, rights and pack scope stay easy to scan.

strengths: The studies materially differ on the named decision: A supports parallel comparison of samples, rights and scope; B prioritizes evaluating one cue before continuing. This is a meaningful priority difference, although no new interaction is established.
A meets the visible placement requirements: the first sample and license conditions share the desktop opening, and all four samples appear in the mobile capture.
Both show disciplined alignment, readable headline wrapping and clear sample actions. B gives the sound itself greater visual authority through waveform scale, contrast and cue-specific context.
The evidence supports a feasible synthesis rather than replacing both directions; neither is ready to expand without repair.
limits: Inspected A desktop, A mobile, B desktop and B mobile in order at native size.
Playback, waveform fidelity, filtering, downloads, keyboard access, contrast compliance and selection behavior remain unverified from still images.
Full license terms, complete pack choices and content below the captures remain unverified.
